adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Washington (state) - Prison section (en.wikipedia.org)
adds.published: 2026-09-19 (revision 1375707468; section reports events of Oct 2023 and Jul 2024)
adds.summary: Prison section: in October 2023, Washington state prisons (under court order and rulings) were legally required to provide gender-affirming healthcare and/or sexual-reassignment surgery to inmates; in July 2024, a trans woman prisoner was transferred from a women's prison back to a men's prison as punishment for consensual sex with a cisgender inmate of the women's prison. Placement outcome documented: birth-sex (men's) housing used as sanction in 2024.

records.note: Placement data found only via the Wikipedia prison section (fetched, HTTP 200, subject-verified). Primary sources cited there — HuffPost, 'Washington Moves Trans Woman Back To Men's Prison In Unprecedented Act' (June 28, 2024) and Pink News, 'Washington prisons must provide gender-affirming care to trans inmates' (Oct 18, 2023) — could not be fetched within budget (direct HuffPost fetch returned 0 bytes; no retries per budget rule), so the Wikipedia article is the sole verified add. No data found within budget on a dedicated special trans unit in Washington DOC or on solitary/segregation practice for trans prisoners.
